text:
harper: Heads up — we started seeing p99 tail spikes on prod around 02:40 UTC. Noticed it after the 02:30 autoscaler/scheduler rollout.

mike: saw that too. overall throughput steady, but latency distribution has a new long tail. p50 ~ stable, p95 up ~10%, p99 doubled.

sasha: initial quick check: KV cache hitrate dips correlated with the spike windows. could be eviction thrash.

jess: can you paste the timeline?

harper: timeline: deploy @02:28, first spike @02:33, repeated spikes every ~3-5min for 30m then subsided at ~03:05.

perf-bot: Incident detected: latency_anomaly service=runtime p99 > 2x baseline for 00:32 minutes.

leo: I pulled profiler traces from a noisy host during a spike. attaching snippet:

```
# top kernel callers (sampled)
lambd_attn_kernel 42%
fused_matmul     18%
kvcache_lookup   12%
other            28%
```

leo: kernel selection looks to be flipping between attn specialized kernel and generic fallback under microbatch sizes ~2-4. That matches the CPU/GPU occupancy oscillation.

mike: microbatch sizing autotuner recently had a subtle change to prefer smaller microbatches to reduce latency for small requests. Could be interacting badly with admission control thresholds.

sasha: admission controller logs show oscillation: admit_rate dropping to 0.2 then back to 1.0 in ~30s cycles. Paste logs: 

```
[02:33:14] admission: in-flight=520 threshold=600 admit=0.88
[02:33:44] admission: in-flight=620 threshold=600 admit=0.21
[02:34:14] admission: in-flight=410 threshold=600 admit=1.00
```

jess: that sawtooth in admit looks like the feedback loop is too aggressive. small microbatches + aggressive admission reduction => underfilled GPU kernels -> kernel selector picks fallback => throughput drop -> queue build -> admission opens -> repeat.

harper: Agreed. Proposed quick mitigation: revert the microbatcher autotuner flag to previous (prefer max_microbatch=8) on the canary pool. Rollout to prod if stable.

mike: I can flip the flag on the canary shard in ~5m. Will monitor p99 and KV cache hit rate.

sasha: before doing that, can we try a daemon-level patch to avoid switching kernel mid-request? Add a hysteresis: require 2 consecutive microbatch-size samples before switching kernel. Should be low-risk.

leo: that's safe. It addresses the kernel-mismatch aspect without changing batching policy. I'll draft a 1-line change in kernel-selector gate.

jess: also let's increase kvcache max_entries by 10% temporarily on affected hosts to reduce eviction churn — low risk.

mike: actioning: 1) flip autotuner flag on canary, 2) bump KV cache entries on canary, 3) watch. If no improvement in 10m, I'll revert and we apply kernel-selector hysteresis.

perf-bot: Runbook note: When p99 spikes with admission oscillation, check microbatcher target and kernel selector toggles.

(10m later)

mike: flipped autotuner flag on canary at 02:52. Initial 6 minutes look promising: p99 dropped ~30%, KV cache hitrate up 4%. Still monitoring.

harper: great. any sign of the admit sawtooth?

mike: sawtooth amplitude reduced, admit_rate now smoother.

leo: I pushed hysteresis patch to a dev branch just in case. jenkins job queued for canary build.

sasha: notes for postmortem: root cause appears to be policy interaction: a recent change to prefer smaller microbatches reduced average microbatch size enough that the kernel selector began to flip between optimized and fallback kernels frequently under load. That flipping combined with aggressive admission control feedback caused underfilling and thrash, which amplified KV cache evictions and pushed tail latency up.

jess: tentative next steps for follow-up:
- run synthetic load with mixed request sizes to reproduce oscillation
- add unit tests for kernel-selector hysteresis
- tune admission control smoothing window (longer averaging)
- evaluate default max_microbatch heuristic (maybe adapt by SLO class)

harper: can someone own the follow-up tickets? I'll open an incident ticket and assign.

mike: I'll own the repro and autotuner revert backstop.

leo: I'll own the kernel-selector hysteresis patch + tests.

sasha: I'll take KV cache tuning and eviction metrics improvements.

jess: I'll draft the postmortem and list the mitigation timeline.

perf-bot: Incident resolved: p99 returned to baseline at 03:05 UTC after canary changes rolled to 10% traffic and admission smoothing.

harper: thanks everyone. We'll do a retro tomorrow at 11am to finalize permanent fixes. :thumbsup:
